Reply ONLY with a compact list: take id, PASS or FAIL, and for FAIL the exact word and how it actually sounded. Do not fail a take for an acceptable alternative pronunciation.

FILE r_bun.wav:
bun00 (0.0-6.9s): "Two parkinsonian syndromes, two classic MRI signs. The hot cross bun, and the hummingbird."
bun01 (8.4-17.5s): "Multiple system atrophy combines parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic failure, like fainting on standing and bladder problems."
bun03 (19.0-27.8s): "On axial T2, that leaves a bright cross in the pons. The hot cross bun sign. The pons and cerebellum also shrink."
bun04 (29.3-34.0s): "It isn't specific. Some spinocerebellar ataxias show it too."
bun05 (35.5-45.5s): "Progressive supranuclear palsy causes early falls, usually backwards, a stiff neck and trunk, and a vertical gaze palsy, especially looking down."
bun06 (47.0-51.5s): "Here the midbrain shrinks, but the pons stays plump."
bun07 (53.0-60.8s): "On the midline sagittal view, the thin midbrain forms the head and beak, and the pons forms the body. That's the hummingbird sign."
bun08 (62.3-67.3s): "On axial images, the same midbrain atrophy gives the Mickey Mouse appearance."
bun09 (68.8-76.7s): "A cross in the pons, think multiple system atrophy. A hummingbird midbrain, think progressive supranuclear palsy."
Key words: atrophy; ataxia; raphe (RAY-fee); pons; spinocerebellar; supranuclear; sagittal (SAJ-ih-tul)

FILE r_mbd.wav:
mbd00 (0.0-6.6s): "Marchiafava-Bignami disease is a rare disorder where the corpus callosum breaks down."
mbd01 (8.1-15.0s): "It's seen mainly in chronic alcohol use disorder and severe malnutrition, and is linked to B vitamin deficiency."
mbd02 (16.5-27.0s): "Patients present with confusion, seizures, trouble walking, or coma. Chronic cases show dementia, and signs of disconnection between the two hemispheres."
mbd03 (28.5-35.3s): "The damage targets the central layers of the corpus callosum, and spares the thin layers above and below."
mbd04 (36.8-44.7s): "On sagittal MRI, that gives the sandwich sign. A bright middle layer on T2 and FLAIR, between preserved darker edges."
mbd05 (46.2-51.7s): "The body is involved most often, then the genu, then the splenium."
mbd06 (53.2-58.0s): "In the acute phase, the callosum is swollen and can restrict diffusion."
mbd07 (59.5-64.5s): "In the chronic phase, it thins out, and develops dark cystic cavities on T1."
mbd08 (66.0-74.4s): "Treatment is thiamine and other B vitamins, plus nutrition and stopping alcohol. Early cases can partly reverse."
mbd09 (75.9-82.4s): "Alcohol history, and a striped corpus callosum? Think Marchiafava-Bignami."
Key words: Marchiafava-Bignami (mar-kee-uh-FAH-vuh been-YAH-mee); corpus callosum (kuh-LOH-sum, long O, NOT kuh-LAH-sum); genu (JEN-yoo); splenium (SPLEE-nee-um); thiamine (THIGH-uh-min); sagittal

FILE r_scd.wav:
scd00 (0.0-6.1s): "Subacute combined degeneration is spinal cord damage from vitamin B twelve deficiency."
scd01 (7.6-17.7s): "Causes include pernicious anemia, stomach or bowel surgery, a strict vegan diet without supplements, and nitrous oxide use, which inactivates B twelve."
scd02 (19.2-28.7s): "B twelve is needed to maintain myelin. Without it, the dorsal columns break down first, then the lateral corticospinal tracts. That's why it's called combined."
scd03 (30.2-39.9s): "The dorsal columns carry vibration and joint position sense. So patients get tingling in the hands and feet, numbness, and an unsteady gait that's worse in the dark."
scd04 (41.4-45.1s): "Corticospinal involvement adds weakness and stiffness."
scd05 (46.6-55.3s): "On sagittal T2, look for a long bright stripe along the back of the cord, usually in the cervical and upper thoracic segments."
scd06 (56.8-65.1s): "On axial T2, the two dorsal columns light up as an inverted V. It's also called the inverted rabbit ears sign."
scd07 (66.6-70.6s): "Copper deficiency can look identical, so check copper too."
scd08 (72.1-78.4s): "Treat early with B twelve replacement. Symptoms and signal changes can reverse if it's caught early."
scd09 (79.9-85.7s): "Sensory ataxia, and an inverted V in the dorsal cord? Check the B twelve."
Key words: subacute; B twelve; pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide; myelin; dorsal; corticospinal; sagittal; cervical; thoracic; ataxia

FILE r_moya.wav:
moya00 (0.0-7.4s): "Moyamoya is a progressive narrowing of the arteries at the base of the brain. The name is Japanese for a puff of smoke."
moya01 (8.9-17.0s): "The ends of both internal carotid arteries slowly narrow, along with the first parts of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries."
moya02 (18.5-25.4s): "To compensate, tiny perforating arteries at the base of the brain enlarge into a tangle of collaterals."
moya03 (26.9-31.6s): "On angiography, that tangle looks like a hazy puff of smoke."
moya04 (33.1-41.7s): "On T2 MRI, look for small or absent flow voids at the carotid ends, and multiple tiny dark dots in the basal ganglia."
moya05 (43.2-51.5s): "On FLAIR and post contrast images, slow flow in pial collaterals outlines the sulci. That's the ivy sign."
moya07 (53.0-62.2s): "When there's no cause, it's moyamoya disease. The same pattern with a cause, like sickle cell disease, neurofibromatosis type one, Down syndrome, or cranial radiation, is moyamoya syndrome."
moya08 (63.7-69.3s): "Treatment is surgical revascularisation, bypassing the narrowing using a scalp artery."
Key words: moyamoya (moy-uh-MOY-uh); carotid (kuh-ROT-id); angiography; pial (PIE-ul or PEE-ul); sulci (SUL-sigh or SUL-kigh); ischemic (iss-KEE-mik); neurofibromatosis; revascularisation
